shareText:
Did you know? 

The Minions almost looked completely different when they were first designed.
During the development of Despicable Me, the filmmakers experimented with many different ideas for Gru's helpers. Early concepts included creatures that looked much more like tiny monsters, but the team felt they were too complicated and not funny enough.

The funniest part is that the final design was intentionally kept as simple as possible: small yellow bodies, blue overalls, goggles, and a language made up of random words mixed with English, Spanish, French, Italian, and gibberish. Even though nobody fully understands what they're saying, millions of fans somehow know exactly what they mean.
Released on July 9, 2010, Despicable Me turned the Minions into global superstars. What started as side characters quickly became so popular that they received their own movies, games, and enough merchandise to fill entire toy stores.

shareText:
Khalil Gibran was a Lebanese-American poet, writer, philosopher, and artist, born in 1883 in the town of Bsharri, Lebanon. He moved to the United States as a young man and became one of the most influential literary figures of the early 20th century. His writing blended Eastern spirituality, Western philosophy, and deep reflections on love, freedom, nature, sorrow, and the human soul. His most famous work, The Prophet (1923), became a timeless spiritual classic, translated into dozens of languages and loved by readers around the world for its poetic wisdom and universal messages.
Gibran’s words often explored the hidden beauty within human experiences — the idea that pain can lead to growth, love can transform the soul, and every person carries a deeper truth within themselves. Through his paintings and writings, he tried to build a bridge between cultures and remind humanity of its shared connection. Like Rumi and other great mystics, Gibran was not only a writer of words but a seeker of meaning, leaving behind a legacy of compassion, imagination, and spiritual insight.
